edits.text: - Keep a numeral or quantifier token (digits or spelled-out number) together with the immediately following measurement unit token or with an immediately following parenthesized measurement phrase that opens with '('; bind the number to that surface-adjacent unit/parenthesis.

- Keep a finite verb or auxiliary (including copula and modals) together with the immediately following span when that next token begins a core complement: 'that' or 'to', a determiner (a/an/the), a pronoun, a numeral, a noun, or an opening parenthesis (keep the verb attached to its complement).

- As a last resort, prefer a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary (comma, semicolon, sentence break) over a cut that splits a numeral/quantifier from its immediately following unit or parenthesized measurement phrase, and over a cut that separates a finite verb/auxiliary from the immediately following phrase that supplies its core complement.

- As a last resort, order candidate cuts on the source surface as follows: prefer a punctuation or clause-boundary cut (comma, semicolon, sentence break) only when that punctuation cut does not split a numeral/quantifier from its immediately following unit or parenthesized measurement phrase, nor separate a finite verb/auxiliary (including copula and modals) from the immediately following phrase that supplies its core complement; if no such punctuation cut exists, prefer the cut that preserves numeral–unit attachment or finite-verb–core-complement attachment over other non-punctuation cuts.

- Prefer a cut that leaves a numeral or quantifier token attached to its immediately following unit or parenthesized measurement phrase over a cut that separates them; and prefer a cut that keeps a finite verb/auxiliary (including copula and modals) attached to the immediately following phrase that supplies its core complement over a cut that separates them.

- Prefer a cut that keeps a numeral or quantifier (digits or spelled-out number) attached to an immediately following parenthesized measurement phrase (an opening '(' within the next two tokens); rank such cuts above alternatives that would split the numeral from that parenthesized unit.
